data.project_sub: ad spot · Solace (named in the idea). End frame: 'Solace. Glazed by hand.' over the used dripper. Design sets the type and layout. · 60s 16:9, 20s 9:16, 15s 9:16, 6s 16:9, 1 still, 3 stills
data.title: Pick the route
data.ask: Approve the strategy and one route. Nothing downstream is built until you do.
open_questions: Does 'one cup at a time' mean it brews a single cup, or that each dripper is glazed one at a time? (A01)
Does the dripper sit straight on a mug with a paper filter? Product photos would settle it. (A02)
Is the plan YouTube plus paid Reels/Stories? (A05)
Is the buyer the parent who drinks the coffee, or someone buying it for them as a gift? (A08)
Live action with the real dripper, or generated scenes around real product shots? (A09)

strategy.proposition: A dripper glazed by hand, for a wait that costs nobody.
strategy.tension: Who: parents who make the day's first coffee at the kitchen counter while the school run gathers behind them. A shoe needs tying, a slip needs signing and their own phone is buzzing, all before the cup is poured. This behavior and moment come from the brief's [audience] field and the premise. They are the client's wish and the film's content, not research. Media proxy: parents of school-age children on Meta Reels/Stories. The two buying cells are defined in assumptions; they are buying assumptions, not research, and H11 decides between them. Tension [H1]: In their voice: I give the kids every other minute of the morning and I don't begrudge them one, yet I want the first coffee to be mine, and I'd hate to admit I'd make them wait for it. What they'd hate to admit: for a few minutes they would put a cup of coffee ahead of their children, and that feels selfish. Asking why once more shows this is about how they see themselves, not about time. Remove the product and the tension still holds, because it is about wanting one thing that is theirs, not about coffee gear. How the proposition settles it. What the film shows (premise content, not proof that it works): the kids wait behind the tape. The teenager, 'without looking up from the phone, she hooks them back behind it with her foot' (premise). Then 'The last drip falls. The parent lifts the dripper off the mug, sets it on the counter, turns, and takes the first sip facing the tape' (premise), and 'they step over it, cup in hand, into everybody talking at once' (story_seed.ending). The end frame is 'the used dripper, grounds still in it, under 'Solace. Glazed by hand.'' (must_include). What we hope viewers conclude: the kids keep the rule themselves [H2], the wait has an end the doorway can see [H5], and the parent goes to them as soon as it ends, so the wait cost nobody [H1(b), H2]. The parent has to believe that conclusion to stop feeling selfish. The film shows it and never says it (taste: restraint over explanation). The end frame then names the dripper by the fact that sets it apart, F3 [H12]. Rejected drafts: H7 (the unused ritual) and H8 (the gift-giver). The price objection is kept as the barrier hypothesis H9, because asking why once more collapses it into H1.

routes.central_idea: The hand-glazed dripper says 'not yet' so the parent never has to; its lift says 'now'.
routes.emotional_promise: The small relief of lifting the dripper off the mug, knowing nobody at the tape ever had to be told no.
routes.product_role: Job: the house's signal. The drain is the 'not yet' nobody has to say out loud, and the lift is the 'now', the sound-off release (A06, H10). [changed] What it costs on F3: any pour-over's drain says 'not yet' (H5). In this idea 'hand-glazed' is the dripper's name, not its logic. First appearance: D01 in use by 4 s (a skippable 16:9 needs it by 5 s). D02 and D03 pouring by 3 s. D04 in frame from the first frame. Brand assets: the dripper itself, the sharpest thing in every waiting frame, with no other object in its glaze colour. No logo anywhere. 'Solace. Glazed by hand.' sits over the used dripper, grounds still in it, for the last 4 s (Design sets the type). [changed] The glaze mark is R1's only Solace-only link, and it depends on a sample nobody has. It is taken only from the A02 sample (an uneven glaze line at the foot, a run, or a bare spot where the dripper was held for dipping). It appears as this dripper's incidental trace of glazing: under the thumb at the lift, in frame at the end. It is never lit, pointed at or held on as a feature. Question for Lucas (A02): does every unit carry a visible glazing mark? If not, a mark shown as the signature implies unit-to-unit variation that F3 doesn't state. Then both the thumb-on-mark beat and the end-frame mark go, and the line carries F3 alone. Nothing may suggest the dripper was formed by hand: no throwing rings, no fingerprints in the clay, no maker at a wheel. Proof: 'The dripper is glazed by hand.' 'Solace makes a ceramic pour-over dripper.' The drain and the silence after the drips are category knowledge (H5), not a claim. Never shown: a lingering shot of steam (heat), a pleased face at the sip (taste), any count of cups (A01). A visible stream appears only if the A02 sample has a window in its base. Every dripper close-up comes from the A02 sample or render. Showing it on the mug waits on A01/A02.
routes.execution_example:
Costs the belief: guarding your coffee means telling the kids no. Keeps: Lucas's seed line and the premise, beat for beat. Subverts: the stolen quiet cup (the house is not off-screen; it waits in the back plane of every frame); the window ritual (overcast light, real time, no steam, no window); the barista bloom (a plain kettle; the one shot into the cone is a draining bed from the parent's eyeline, not a macro of the bloom). Look: 50mm locked-off at counter height, the dripper sharp in front, the doorway behind; overcast window camera left, 5600K, 3:1; #2E6FB7 tape, #EFE8DA mug.

routes.central_idea: The quiet isn't taken, it's given: small hands lay the tape for the hand-glazed dripper.
routes.emotional_promise: The sheepish gratitude of stepping over a fresh strip of tape a seven-year-old pressed flat for you this morning.
routes.product_role: [changed: new route] Job: what the wait is given to. The kids lay the tape and stand behind it. The dripper is the one thing beyond the line they don't interrupt, and the sharpest thing past it in every hall-side frame. F3 is part of the logic: the film shows two pairs of hands before the line names a third. A small hand lays the rule, the parent's hands pour, and 'Glazed by hand' names the one step in the dripper's making that was done by hand (F3), and no more. It needs no glaze mark, so it does not wait on A02 for one. First appearance: in D01 it is pouring by 4 s, seen beyond the tape (a skippable 16:9 needs it by 5 s). D02 and D03 pouring by 3 s. D04 in frame from the first frame. Brand assets: the dripper, sharp beyond the tape. No logo anywhere. 'Solace. Glazed by hand.' sits over the used dripper, grounds still in it, with the fresh strip empty behind it, for the last 4 s. Proof: 'The dripper is glazed by hand.' 'Solace makes a ceramic pour-over dripper.' Nothing may suggest the dripper was formed by hand: no throwing rings, no fingerprints in the clay, no maker at a wheel. The small hand touches only the tape, never the dripper. Never shown: a lingering shot of steam (heat), a pleased face at the sip (taste), any count of cups (A01). The drips are heard, not seen, unless A02 shows a window in the base. Close-ups come from A02 only. Showing it on the mug waits on A01/A02.
routes.execution_example:
[changed: new route] Costs the belief: a parent's quiet has to be taken from the kids. Keeps: Lucas's seed line and every object and beat of the premise. Adds (questions for Lucas): a small hand laying the fresh strip at 0 s, which makes the rule the kids' doing; the empty charging cable; the reach past the lit phone to the pen as the hero payoff. Subverts: the stolen quiet cup (the quiet isn't stolen; the kids lay it down); the window ritual (we watch from the dim hall, and the window is only the kitchen's light); the barista bloom (the dripper is seen from 3 m, the way the kids see it, not in macro). Pairing: R1's frame never shows who lays the tape, so it can't carry 'given, not taken'. R2's example puts the rule in a child's hand at 0 s and holds the wait from her side, so it doesn't serve R1's idea either: here the kids say 'not yet', not the dripper. Against R3: no queue, and no serving after the step-over. Shared only because the brief sets them: the lift as the cue (A06) and D04's content. Risk (A07, H2): a child laying painter's tape may push the 'paint' reading, so the H2 mock-up must include the laying. Look: 85mm locked-off from the hall behind the tape, the held thing soft and the dripper sharp beyond; a counter-side reverse from the lift; kitchen window 5600K, the hall 4:1; #2E6FB7 tape, #E3B23C sock. routes.central_idea: Parents go last, except at the counter: the hand-glazed dripper is first in the morning's line.
routes.emotional_promise: The guilt-free pleasure of going first: the first sip taken facing the line, then the line served, cup in hand.
routes.product_role: Job: first in line. The dripper heads the morning's queue, nearest the lens, and is dealt with before anything held at the tape. Everything after it gets one hand, because the cup is in the other. First appearance: in D01 it is pouring by 4 s at the head of the line. D02 and D03 pouring by 3 s. D04 in frame from the first frame. Brand assets: the dripper nearest the lens at frame left in every wide of the line. The end frame goes back to the head of the line: 'Solace. Glazed by hand.' over the used dripper, grounds still in it, for the last 4 s. R1's glaze-mark rule and its A02 question apply: the mark is incidental, never a feature, and without a mark the line carries F3 alone. Nothing may suggest the dripper was formed by hand: no throwing rings, no fingerprints in the clay, no maker at a wheel. Proof: 'The dripper is glazed by hand.' 'Solace makes a ceramic pour-over dripper.' Never shown: lingering steam, any sip that reads as praise for the coffee, any count of cups. Close-ups come from A02 only. Showing it on the mug waits on A01/A02.
routes.execution_example:
Costs the belief: a good parent goes last. Keeps: Lucas's seed line, and shows in picture what it only implies, that the parent goes first. Adds a post-release sequence not in the premise, the parent serving the line; that is a question for Lucas. Subverts: the stolen quiet cup (the parent goes first in the open, at the head of the queue); the window ritual (before sunrise, a pendant over the counter, windows dark); the barista bloom (a wide where the product is a place in a line). Pairing: against R1, the dripper is a position in a queue, not a signal the doorway watches, and the film runs 20 s past the release. Against R2, nobody lays the tape on camera, and every object is served in queue order. Look: 35mm three-quarter on, the line receding from the dripper to the tape, framed chest down until the step-over; locked-off, then a dolly; pendant 3200K top-down, 2:1, windows dark. Tags as in R1.

With the sound off, the lift carries the cue (H10). Cut in: the parent turns and takes the first sip facing the line.

data.recommendation:
Pick R1. The proposition, 'A dripper glazed by hand, for a wait that costs nobody', lands at 43-52 s. The hand waits until the drips stop and lifts the dripper, and the parent turns to sip facing the tape without having refused anyone. With the dripper the sharpest thing in every waiting frame, R1 best serves the pre-flight criterion (4 of 5 muted viewers call 'now' at the lift and name the dripper) and D02's lift-reach rate. D02 is the cut it serves, and its master frame gives S01 and D04 as labelled.
Gives up [changed]: F3 doing any work. R2 builds 'by hand' into the story: a small hand lays the rule, the parent's hands pour, and the line names the glaze. R1 trades that for the clearest muted release. R1 also fails the rival swap test until A02 and H4 are answered, because its drain says 'not yet' for any pour-over (H5), and its only Solace-only link, the glaze mark, depends on a sample nobody has. It gives up the open admission that the parent goes first (R3). The hook-back reads on an insert, not in the main frame.
Failure: D02 17-20 s (D01 56-60 s). At phone size the glaze mark can read as a chip in a film that has already shown a chipped mug. The fix comes in stages. (1) The mug has left in the parent's hand, so nothing chipped shares the end frame. (2) The window key rakes across the glaze so the mark reads as glaze, without framing it larger than the grounds. (3) Check it in the H12 viewing. (4) If it still reads as damage, drop it from the end frame; the thumb at the lift keeps it in the film, and the line carries F3 alone. If A02 shows that not every unit carries a mark, both go before the shoot.
Kill test [changed]: the muted D02 first cut gets 'now' at the lift, but viewers say the parent is ignoring the kids, not that the kids are waiting for the parent to finish. The drain is reading as the parent's no, so the idea fails, not the craft. Switch to R3. Its post-release line, with the parent serving each held thing in turn, cup in hand, is the only route that shows the wait cost nobody. R2 would not fix it: it answers who set the rule, not whether the parent pays the wait back.
Case R2 [changed]: H2 (must_include A07), punishment answers. If the silent doorway mock-up gets 'they're being made to stand there', A07's fallback still triggers, as the brief sets. R2 is the route to carry into that retest, because it is the only one that shows in picture who lays the tape. It does nothing for 'paint' answers and may add to them; those stay with A07's fallback alone. Also H3: if gifts are most orders (H8), 'given, not taken' re-aims at the giver with the least rework.
Case R3 [changed]: audience_tension H1(b). If the H1(b)/H2 viewing survives with three or more of six parents calling the doorway parent 'selfish' or 'shutting them out', the guilt is live and the release alone won't settle it. R3 admits the parent goes first and pays the line back, object by object. If H1(b) dies, R3 has no guilt left to answer either.
